## Recurrence Hotspots
- **error-handling in IPC bridge and its async consumers** — 12 of 46 total threads across both PRs concern error handling around the Rust↔TS IPC boundary, its async listener wiring, or its client-side state machine (parse validation, partial reads, default branches, async-cleanup races, missing `.catch`, type-validation, mid-flight state mutation, HMR listener accumulation, temp-file collision FUD). Suggested preventive action: when introducing a new event surface OR a new async-resolved listener in this codebase, the default/unknown branch, the type guard, the cleanup hook, AND any client-state-guard ("disabled while running") should be in the same commit as the surface — not as follow-up review-cycle fixes.
- **Trust-boundary validation at the periphery** — 7 PR-2 threads across data-integrity (GPS truthiness, duplicates naming, `loadSettings` no validation, fade-duration `0`-as-falsy) all trace to the same root cause: trusting whatever the boundary handed back. PR-1 had the parallel symptom (`"type": 42` accepted as event). **Suggestion:** when reading from any external source (localStorage, IPC, EXIF, user input), write the per-field type/range guard in the same commit as the read. The guard belongs at the boundary, not later in the consumer.
